paper_summary: Finite-element (Abaqus/Explicit) study of aluminium (Al6061) automotive crash boxes (70 x 70 x 200 mm) filled with glass-microballoon/epoxy syntactic foam in six filling configurations (full, 1/2, 1/4, empty, 8 mm and 16 mm lateral wall thickness), impacted by a rigid wall at 64 km/h for 5 ms. No foams were manufactured or tested: the syntactic-foam elastic constants (density 0.3 g/cm3, E = 1650 MPa, nu = 0.2) and Johnson-Cook plasticity constants were taken from / fitted to literature data (Li et al., Mater. Sci. Eng. A 515, 19 (2009)). The FEA shows that increasing foam fill lowers crash-box displacement, that full filling gives the highest (undesirable) initial reaction force, and that lateral-wall foam filling (Cases 5 and 6) gives the best compromise of energy absorption and reaction force at little weight penalty.

extraction_notes: This is a pure finite-element / light-weighting design study; the authors manufactured and tested no syntactic foam themselves, so no primary Process-Structure-Property data exist. The only quantitative foam material data are the FE material cards in Tables III and IV, both attributed to ref. [11] (P. Li, N. Petrinic, C.R. Siviour, R. Froud, J.M. Reed, Mater. Sci. Eng. A 515, 19 (2009)); Table III is tagged data_origin='secondary' (values quoted from that paper) and Table IV 'model' (Johnson-Cook constants the present authors calculated/fitted). The paper states only 'micro glass bubble/epoxy' - no microballoon grade, volume/weight fraction, particle size or processing route is given, so those fields are null and process_route is set to 'other'. Table IV as printed has 6 parameter columns but only 5 numbers, so the exponent m is missing; A=15 MPa, B=0.01 MPa, n=0.0001, C=0.105, eps_dot_0=3500 1/s is the alignment implied by the running text. strength_mpa=15 records the Johnson-Cook A constant and should be treated as a constitutive parameter, not a measured strength; the test_type 'compression' and strain rate 3500 1/s reflect the reference strain rate of that card. All FEA outputs (maximum displacement, reaction force, impact load-deformation, absorbed energy for Cases 1-6, Figs. 4-6) are presented only as plots with no tabulated numbers, so they were not extracted; Table V gives only the foam mass per case (288, 144, 72, -, 119, 207 g) for a 70x70x200 mm Al6061 crash box, which is geometry rather than a material property. Al6061 Johnson-Cook parameters (Tables I and II) belong to the crash-box metal, not to a syntactic foam, and were not extracted.
